technical_and_design_decisions: The increment targets the Spring XD codebase (streams, modules, containers, admin), built on Spring Integration (SI), Spring AMQP, Spring Data, and Spring Boot, per the user stories.

U1: Implement the alternative DLQ as a per-module/per-stream configuration option in the message bus/binder layer; on failure, republish the original message to the configured alternative DLQ with added headers carrying the exception class, message, and a serialized stack trace, reusing the existing Spring Integration error-handling infrastructure.

U2: Deliver Change Data Capture (CDC) as an out-of-the-box source module that emits database change events into a stream; downstream destinations (brokers, Hadoop, DBs) are served by existing sink modules, so only the source/capture side and event serialization are built. A log/trigger-based CDC approach is wrapped behind a module API with configuration metadata.

U3: Support RabbitMQ HA/FT by accepting a comma-separated list of cluster node addresses in the connection configuration with automatic failover across nodes; implement the multi-address support in Spring AMQP usage (upstream-compatible) and expose it through the XD Rabbit binder properties.
U4: Align the build with Spring Data Gosling GA and upgrade the Gemfire dependency to 8.1, migrating any code affected by API changes and regression-testing Gemfire source/sink/analytics modules.

U5: Add a colocated stream deployment option so all modules of a stream run inside a single container JVM; implement leader election using the existing ZooKeeper infrastructure (Curator-style recipes) so a colocated stream fails over automatically to another container.
U6/U7: Perform version upgrades of Spring Integration and SI Kafka extensions, adapting to API/behavior changes and validating the JMX and Kafka improvements; no new features beyond synchronization.
U8: Upgrade to Spring Boot 1.2.3 and align dependency management with spring-boot-dependencies by updating the 28 listed managed versions, resolving resulting incompatibilities.
assumptions: Despite the generic Spring Framework 6.0 introduction, the user stories describe a Spring XD increment of the Boot 1.2.x era (Java 7/8); estimates are made for that codebase and toolchain.
A single developer performs all work; all figures are effort in work-hours, not elapsed calendar time.
Externally released dependencies (SI milestone/GA, Spring Data Gosling GA, Gemfire 8.1, Boot 1.2.3, SI Kafka) are already available when work begins; no idle waiting time is included.

Existing build, CI, and test infrastructure is available; integration-test resources (multi-node RabbitMQ cluster, supported databases, ZooKeeper ensemble, Gemfire) can be provisioned in the existing test environment.

Effort estimates include analysis/design, implementation, unit and integration testing, documentation/release notes, and code review with rework; they exclude project management, production deployment, and end-user training.
The CDC source module targets a defined set of mainstream relational databases (e.g., MySQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle) via the chosen CDC approach, not arbitrary databases.
Destinations for CDC events (brokers, Hadoop, DBs) are handled by composing existing XD sink modules; no new sinks are built.
Leader election reuses the ZooKeeper infrastructure already present in XD; no new consensus system is introduced.
No changes to third-party library internals are required beyond version alignment and configuration; the Rabbit HA improvement is implemented within XD/spring-amqp usage scope.
